introduction: Work First is North Carolina’s TANF family-assistance program. It combines temporary support with employment services.
description: Work First is North Carolina’s TANF family-assistance program. It combines temporary support with employment services.

sections.who: County DSS checks family and financial rules. The wider service income threshold is not necessarily the cash-benefit threshold.
sections.get: Qualifying families may receive cash, diversion, emergency or supportive services. Availability depends on the category.
sections.docs:
• Child and household information.
  • Income and resource records.
  • Requested residency and eligibility proof.
sections.apply:
1. Apply

    Use ePASS or county DSS.

  2. Discuss options

    Ask about Benefit Diversion or Emergency Assistance for short-term needs.

  3. Complete the plan

    Follow the Mutual Responsibility Agreement and relevant work requirements.
sections.after: Ask about time limits and exemptions; report changes and retain notices.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using Work First services and application; Eligibility. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Is the broad service income limit the cash limit?
No. Ask DSS for the applicable category.
Ask the county before selecting ongoing assistance.
Work First lists a Mutual Responsibility Agreement.
Can relatives caring for children seek help?
The program includes relevant relative-caregiver support.
